subject.title: fix(agents): bound finished bash process session retention

question: Should completed process poll/log records be allowed to expire before their TTL once the new 50-session or 2,000,000-character budget is reached?
rationale: The resource bound fixes a real availability problem but deliberately changes how long completed process output remains pollable under burst load; tests cannot determine whether those thresholds match the intended operator contract.

options.title: Accept bounded early eviction
options.body: Keep the proposed internal limits, require live gateway proof, and document in PR context that resource budgets may evict completed records before TTL.

options.title: Revise the retention policy
options.body: Adjust the limits or eviction behavior and add focused coverage for the maintainer-selected delayed-poll contract before merging.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded early eviction
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed internal limits, require live gateway proof, and document in PR context that resource budgets may evict completed records before TTL.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent exec lifecycle merger and the strongest available routing candidate for accepting the runtime compatibility tradeoff.
